scenes.tts: Push a tiny bead into a chick embryo's forebrain. The bead is soaked in one protein, F G F eight. A second midbrain can grow there, built back to front. How can one bead do that? Cells in the neural tube must know where they sit. Who tells them?

scenes.visual: Neural tube; bead drops into forebrain, a second green midbrain grows around it; question marks over the cells.
scenes.narration: Push a tiny bead into a chick embryo's forebrain. The bead is soaked in one protein, FGF8. A second midbrain can grow there, built back to front. How can one bead do that? Cells in the neural tube must know where they sit. Who tells them?

scenes.tts: Hox genes give the hindbrain and spinal cord their addresses. But the midbrain and forebrain have no Hox code at all. They need other instructions. Where do those come from? A local organizer is a small signaling center inside the neural tube. It tells the cells around it what to build.
scenes.visual: Hox bars over the hindbrain, empty over fore and midbrain; a yellow organizer appears at the isthmus and arrows go out to neighbours.
scenes.narration: Hox genes give the hindbrain and spinal cord their addresses. But the midbrain and forebrain have no Hox code at all. They need other instructions. Where do those come from? A local organizer is a small signaling center inside the neural tube. It tells the cells around it what to build.

scenes.tts: The best studied sits where the midbrain meets the hindbrain, at a narrowing called the isthmus. Two transcription factors draw the line. O T X two is on in the forebrain and midbrain. G B X two is on in the front of the hindbrain. Each represses the other, so the edge between them is sharp.
scenes.caption: The best studied sits where the midbrain meets the hindbrain, at a narrowing called the isthmus. Two transcription factors draw the line. OTX2 is on in the forebrain and midbrain. GBX2 is on in the front of the hindbrain. Each represses the other, so the edge between them is sharp.
scenes.visual: Two coloured bars meet at the isthmus; two blunt-ended arrows push against each other and the edge sharpens.
scenes.narration: The best studied sits where the midbrain meets the hindbrain, at a narrowing called the isthmus. Two transcription factors draw the line. OTX2 is on in the forebrain and midbrain. GBX2 is on in the front of the hindbrain. Each represses the other, so the edge between them is sharp.

scenes.tts: At that line, a set of genes switches on and keeps itself going. F G F eight forms a band just behind the boundary. Wint one forms a ring just in front. Engrailed and Pax two and Pax five span the boundary. In the standard model, each helps keep the others on. Remove one, and the rest fade.

scenes.visual: Stripes appear in the tube; three chips joined in a loop; one chip is crossed out and the other two fade.
scenes.narration: At that line, a set of genes switches on and keeps itself going. FGF8 forms a band just behind the boundary. Wnt1 forms a ring just in front. Engrailed and Pax2 and Pax5 span the boundary. In the standard model, each helps keep the others on. Remove one, and the rest fade.

scenes.tts: Is that enough to organize? This tests sufficiency. Put an F G F eight bead in the forebrain. Cells next to it turn on Engrailed. Later they form a midbrain. The new midbrain is a mirror image. Parts that normally lie nearest the isthmus form nearest the bead. Parts from farther forward form farther away. That is what you expect if cells read their distance from a source.

scenes.tts: Now test necessity by removing the signal. Mouse embryos with no Wint one lack the midbrain and much of the cerebellum. Mice that make greatly reduced F G F eight lose the midbrain and cerebellum too. Add a factor where it is absent, and the structure forms. Remove it, and the structure is lost. You need both tests.
